Definition: from a compound of G3844 and G1685; a throwing in beside (juxtaposition), i.e. (specially), battle-array, encampment or barracks (tower Antonia):--army, camp, castle.
BiblicalUsage: Parembole is the camp, the barracks, the army drawn up in battle. In Acts the word is the castle in Jerusalem where Paul is held: the chief captain takes him into the castle in Acts 21:37, and the soldiers carry him there in Acts 23:10. Hebrews 11:34 remembers those who through faith waxed valiant in fight and turned to flight the armies of the aliens, and Hebrews 13:11 says the bodies of the beasts whose blood is brought into the sanctuary are burned without the camp.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the camp is where the army sleeps and where the sacrifice is burned, and the gospel sends us both places: into the fight of faith, and outside the camp to bear Christ's reproach. I hold that outside the camp is where Christ suffered, and the camp I am called out of is the one that would keep me comfortable and far from Him.
